The test image shows corn leaves with reddish-brown, powdery pustules breaking through the leaf surface. There are also yellow-orange halos around some lesions. This is clearly a rust disease. The pustules are reddish-brown and somewhat large/irregular, suggesting Common Rust over Southern Rust (which tends to be smaller, more orange, and on upper surface only).

Let me view one Common Rust reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows early-stage Common Rust with small, elongated orange-red pustules. The test image shows a more advanced/heavy infection with coalesced, reddish-brown powdery pustules erupting through the leaf surface — consistent with mature Common Rust (Puccinia sorghi), which produces brick-red to cinnamon-brown uredinia on both leaf surfaces. The yellow-orange halo areas also match.
